original_review_text:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR11496
family_name: ALCOHOL DEHYDROGENASE
preferred_name: Iron-activated (group III) alcohol dehydrogenases and related Fe-ADH-fold oxidoreductases
summary: >-
  Members of the iron-containing alcohol dehydrogenase fold (group III ADHs), unrelated in
  structure to the zinc medium-chain ADHs. Characterized NAD(H)-dependent alcohol
  dehydrogenases in the family include Zymomonas mobilis ADH II (adhB), the major fermentative
  ADH of that bacterium; S. cerevisiae ADH4, a minor, zinc-induced isozyme reported as
  mitochondrial; fission yeast adh4, a mitochondrial-matrix ethanol dehydrogenase that also
  sustains ethanol fermentation in adh1 null cells; E. coli FucO (lactaldehyde reductase),
  EutG, YiaY and the alcohol dehydrogenase domain of AdhE; and Klebsiella/Citrobacter
  1,3-propanediol dehydrogenase DhaT. The same fold is used by enzymes that are not ordinary
  alcohol dehydrogenases: maleylacetate reductases of chloroaromatic degradation, methanol:
  N,N-dimethyl-4-nitrosoaniline oxidoreductases, sulfoacetaldehyde and phosphonoacetaldehyde
  reductases, Kdo 8-oxidase (KdnB), and the animal mitochondrial hydroxyacid-oxoacid
  transhydrogenase ADHFE1.
functional_coherence: HETEROGENEOUS
coherence_reason: >-
  The fold and a metal-assisted hydride transfer are shared, but substrates and even reaction
  types differ between and within subfamilies. SF102 (ALCOHOL DEHYDROGENASE 4) contains the
  yeast ADH4/adh4 and Zymomonas AdhB ethanol dehydrogenases together with maleylacetate
  reductases, methanol:NDMA oxidoreductases, 1,3-propanediol dehydrogenases and choline
  dehydrogenase GbsB. SF83 mixes bacterial AdhE/PduQ alcohol dehydrogenases with the
  eukaryotic hydroxyacid-oxoacid transhydrogenase ADHFE1. Ethanol dehydrogenase activity
  belongs to particular clades that the PANTHER subfamilies do not separate cleanly.

    adh4) and Zymomonas AdhB, the members used by the alcoholic fermentation module, but also
    maleylacetate reductases, methanol:NDMA oxidoreductases, 1,3-propanediol dehydrogenases,
    4-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase, choline dehydrogenase GbsB and E. coli YiaY.
  representative_members:

    gene_symbol: ADH4

  - id: UniProtKB:Q09669
    label: Alcohol dehydrogenase 4
    gene_symbol: adh4
    organism: Schizosaccharomyces pombe
    gene_review: genes/SCHPO/adh4/adh4-ai-review.yaml
  - id: UniProtKB:P0DJA2
    label: Alcohol dehydrogenase 2
    gene_symbol: adhB
    organism: Zymomonas mobilis subsp. mobilis
  diverged_from_family: false
  supported_by:

    supporting_text: This is the first observation that a S. cerevisiae ADH4-like alcohol
      dehydrogenase functions in yeast ethanol fermentation.
- subfamily_id: PANTHER:PTHR11496:SF83
  label: HYDROXYACID-OXOACID TRANSHYDROGENASE, MITOCHONDRIAL
  description: >-
    Bacterial bifunctional aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenases (AdhE), propanol dehydrogenase PduQ,
    Clostridium butanol and 4-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenases, Entamoeba ADH2, together with
    the animal and Dictyostelium mitochondrial hydroxyacid-oxoacid transhydrogenases (ADHFE1).
  representative_members:
  - id: UniProtKB:P0A9Q7
    label: Bifunctional aldehyde-alcohol dehydrogenase AdhE
    gene_symbol: adhE
    organism: Escherichia coli K-12
  - id: UniProtKB:Q8IWW8
    label: Hydroxyacid-oxoacid transhydrogenase, mitochondrial
    gene_symbol: ADHFE1
    organism: Homo sapiens
  diverged_from_family: true
  divergence_description: >-
    Mixed. The eukaryotic ADHFE1 clade is named and annotated as a hydroxyacid-oxoacid
    transhydrogenase (coupling 4-hydroxybutyrate oxidation to 2-oxoglutarate reduction), not as
    a free-NAD+ ethanol dehydrogenase, and is mitochondrial; the bacterial members are
    alcohol dehydrogenases. Neither ethanol dehydrogenase nor transhydrogenase terms are safe
    at subfamily level.

  assessment: UNRESOLVED
  assessment_reason: >-
    The seeds span SF102, SF83 and SF94, so the node is placed near the family root and the
    IBA reaches 131 proteins, including the S. cerevisiae ADH4 and fission yeast adh4 members
    used by the alcoholic fermentation module (both reviews accept it, with purified-enzyme or
    mitochondrial activity data). It also reaches the animal hydroxyacid-oxoacid
    transhydrogenases (human ADHFE1 and orthologs, SF83), FucO (SF106), KdnB (SF104) and GbsB.
    For the yeast members the placement is sound. For ADHFE1 the transferred term looks like an
    over-propagation onto a transhydrogenase, but no gene review in this repository has
    examined ADHFE1, so this is recorded as unresolved rather than as a pruning call.

    label: ethanol dehydrogenase (NAD+) activity
  scope: SUBFAMILY_ONLY
  scope_reason: >-
    The term the alcoholic fermentation module requires of this family. Established for the
    ADH4-type yeast enzymes and Zymomonas AdhB, all in SF102. SF102 also contains maleylacetate
    reductases, methanol:NDMA oxidoreductases and other non-ethanol enzymes that PANTHER does not
    split off, so the term is safe only for the ADH4/AdhB clade within SF102, not for every
    SF102 member. Not safe for SF83, SF94, SF104, SF106 or SF107 as subfamilies.

    id: GO:0004022

- assessed_term:
    id: GO:0047577
    label: 4-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase activity
  scope: SUBFAMILY_ONLY
  scope_reason: >-
    The term the bacterial 4-hydroxybutyrate oxidation module requires of this family. It is
    established for Cupriavidus necator GHBDH (Q59104) in SF102, whose recombinant enzyme was assayed
    in the alcohol-to-aldehyde direction with NAD and whose Fe2+ chelators and candidate general base

    split, so the term is safe only for the GHBDH-type clade within it and not for every SF102 member;
    a member needs its own substrate evidence, since group III Fe-ADH architecture alone does not pick
    out 4-hydroxybutyrate. Not safe for SF83, SF94, SF104, SF106 or SF107 as subfamilies.
  applicable_subfamilies:
  - id: PANTHER:PTHR11496:SF102
    label: ALCOHOL DEHYDROGENASE 4

      PP_2650 shares SF102 with GHBDH but its 4-hydroxybutyrate assignment comes only from the
      unreviewed submitter name and the EC mapping derived from it. The work on 1,4-butanediol

      dehydrogenase assays on extracts, so its review marks the substrate-specific term as an
      over-annotation while keeping the alcohol-dehydrogenase class.
    supported_by:

    - reference_id: PMID:32256468
      supporting_text: Attempts to obtain direct biochemical evidence for the oxidation hypothesis with
  supported_by:

  - reference_id: file:genes/CUPNE/gbd/gbd-ai-review.yaml
    supporting_text: The oxidoreductase activity is resolved to reversible 4-hydroxybutyrate oxidation.
- assessed_term:
    id: GO:0003858
    label: 3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase activity
  scope: SUBFAMILY_ONLY
  scope_reason: >-
    The comparative activity the same module records for P. putida KT2440 PP_2049 (Q88L86), also in
    SF102, whose purified protein was assayed on (R)-3-hydroxybutyrate with NAD and shown by deletion
    to be the main route to acetoacetate, ahead of the canonical SDR-family HbdH (PP_3073). The SF102

    boundary rather than a property of all SF102 members, and 3-hydroxybutyrate and 4-hydroxybutyrate

    3-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenases are short-chain dehydrogenases outside this family altogether,
    which is why this is not a family-wide expectation.

  - reference_id: file:genes/PSEPK/PP_2049/PP_2049-ai-review.yaml
    supporting_text: equimolar NADH and acetoacetate (AA) were generated for both PP_2049 and PP_3073
- assessed_term:
    id: GO:0005739
    label: mitochondrion
  scope: UNRESOLVED
  scope_reason: >-
    Through PAINT only for the eukaryotic ADHFE1 clade of SF83. The fungal ADH4-type enzymes in
    SF102 are also mitochondrial (fission yeast adh4 in the matrix; S. cerevisiae ADH4 by
    localization studies), but that comes from their own data, not from inheritance. SF83 and
    SF102 are both mixed for this location, so a subfamily scope would be too broad.

notes: >-
  Node membership read from the PAINT UniProt GAF. Both S. cerevisiae ADH4 and fission yeast
  adh4 are described as mitochondrial in their gene reviews, whereas the alcoholic fermentation
  module frames the iron ADH variant as a cytosolic-pathway back-up. The module does not state
  a location for this variant, so there is no direct contradiction, but the module text could
  note the mitochondrial localization. S. cerevisiae ADH4 was reported to be zinc- rather than
  iron-activated (PMID:3282541), so the module's "iron-activated" label is a family-level
  description, not a property verified for ADH4. No residue sites asserted.
